summary: `run: proxy` makes one outbound GET or POST and streams the answer to the caller as the flow's response, for bytes `run: api` cannot carry (it reads at most 1 MiB, as text): text-to-speech audio, a PDF or CSV an outside service generates, an image fetched for CORS or mixed-content reasons, a download kept behind the flow's own checks. It is a terminal step like respond and serve_file. It is not a general reverse proxy: one request, the author's host, allow-listed media types only.
yaml_example:
# flows/speak.yaml - text to speech, the audio streamed to the caller
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/speak/:voice_id
    auth: required
    rate_limit: "30/hour per user"     # every proxied byte is outbound bandwidth

jobs:
  speak:
    steps:
      - run: proxy
        with:
          url: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/${{ params.voice_id }}
          method: POST
          headers:
            xi-api-key: "${{ env.ELEVENLABS_KEY }}"
          json:
            text: "${{ params.text }}"
            model_id: eleven_multilingual_v2
          content_types: [audio/mpeg]
          max_bytes: 20MB
          timeout: 30s
          filename: speech.mp3
keys: Each key of the step (`url`, `path_slashes`, `method`, `headers`, `auth`, `content_types`, `max_bytes`, `timeout`, `disposition`, `filename`, `cache_control`) is in the topic key `proxy_keys`: api({at:'flows.proxy_keys'}).
response: What the caller receives, and every way the step fails before or during the stream, is in the topic key `proxy_response`: api({at:'flows.proxy_response'}).
where: A synchronous `on: request` flow only. Refused when written (and when run) in `mode: async`, scheduled and data-event flows, in an `on_error:` handler, inside `run: parallel`, and in a `transaction: true` flow (its answer is held until commit, and a stream cannot be). Also refused when written (and when loaded) inside `for_each:`, at any depth: the step answers once and ends the flow, so a loop would stop after its first item. Inside `if:` it may run; a failure there reports the proxy step's own failed_step, failed_type and reason. Steps after an unconditional proxy step cannot run and are refused, as after respond. A flow anonymous callers can run (`auth: none`, `optional` or unset, with no `role:` or `permissions:`) must declare `on.request.rate_limit` (e.g. `"30/minute per ip"`), refused when written otherwise: without one the route is an open bandwidth relay to your upstream account.
not_included: No server-side result cache and no per-plan bandwidth metering: every proxied byte is the app's outbound bandwidth, every call goes to the upstream. Bound abuse with `on.request.rate_limit` and `auth: required`. No Range requests (seeking re-downloads), no `sign:` recipes (use `headers:`/`auth:` with env credentials), no `query:` map (write the query in the URL), and no cross-host redirect allow-list.
browser: Show or download it: make it a GET flow and point an element at the flow's URL: ``, `

Read the bytes in page code: `const blob = await bm.flows.avatar({ id: 7 })` resolves a Blob for an image, audio, PDF or ZIP answer and the text for a text/* answer such as CSV; show a Blob with `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` and release it with `URL.revokeObjectURL`. A non-2xx answer throws (err.status, err.message). For a GET flow, params that no `:path` segment uses are sent as the query string (`bm.flows.avatar({ id: 7, size: 64 })` requests `/api/avatar/7?size=64`) and the generated type takes no body. See api({at:'sdk'}) → response_bodies.

A POST proxy flow (text to speech) needs code: `const audio = await bm.flows.speak({ voice_id: 'v1' }, { text }); player.src = URL.createObjectURL(audio);`. bm.flows sends the CSRF token; plain `fetch` must send `X-CSRF-Token` (from `<meta name="csrf-token">`) and `credentials: 'same-origin'`, check `res.ok`, then read `await res.blob()`.
